conceptual assets.concept: Stored counter values (cycle, instret, and HPM counters) used for counting and CSR readback
conceptual assets.reasoning: The counter value is stored and updated inside the counter sub-block and exported for CSR readback: low_reg writes or updates the low word (`if (we_i='1') and (sel_i='0') then lo_q <= wdata_i(...) else lo_q <= nxt(...)`); `nxt <= ... + unsigned(inc)` and `inc <= (others => inc_i)` implement the increment; high_reg accumulates carry into `hi_q`. The sub-block output_select drives the sub-block `rdata_o` from `lo_q`/`hi_q` when `re_i='1'`. Top-level instances map the sub-block `inc_i` to `cnt_en(i)` and their `rdata_o` into `cycle_rd`/`instret_rd`/`hpmcnt(i)`, and the module output is `rdata_o <= cycle_rd or time_rd or instret_rd or hpm_rd`. These RTL relations show the stored registers and exit ports realize the counted value; corrupting the registers or their readback ports would violate the implemented counting and readback behavior (Integrity).

conceptual assets.concept: HPM event configuration registers (hpmevent[i]) that select which events HPM counters count
conceptual assets.reasoning: Each hpmevent(i) is a stored configuration written from the CSR write data when its write qualifier is asserted: in hpmevent_reg `if (cfg_we(i) = '1') then hpmevent(i) <= ctrl_i.csr_wdata(11 downto 0)`. The cnt_control process uses hpmevent(i) in the enable equation `cnt_en(i) <= or_reduce_f(ctrl_i.cnt_event and hpmevent(i)) ...`, so hpmevent bits determine which event signals enable HPM increments. The RTL therefore establishes hpmevent as a configuration whose corruption changes counting behavior (Integrity).

conceptual assets.concept: CSR decode and gating decisions that qualify CSR reads/writes to counters or hpmevent registers
conceptual assets.reasoning: CSR access qualification is computed in the generate and assignment logic: `sel(i) <= '1' when (ctrl_i.csr_addr(3 downto 0) = to_unsigned(i,4)) else '0'`; `cnt_we(i) <= cnt_acc and sel(i) and ctrl_i.csr_we`; `cnt_acc` is set when `ZICNTR_EN` and `ctrl_i.csr_addr(11 downto 5)` matches the cycle/mcycle address region; `cfg_acc` is set similarly for mhpmevent region. These computed signals determine whether a CSR read/write targets a counter or an hpmevent register; their incorrect setting would misroute reads/writes and break the module's CSR semantics (Integrity).

conceptual assets.concept: Per-counter enable bits (cnt_en) that gate increments
conceptual assets.reasoning: The per-counter enable vector is stored and updated in cnt_control: on reset `cnt_en <= (others => '0')`; on clock `cnt_en(0) <= ctrl_i.cnt_event(cnt_event_cy_c) and (not ctrl_i.cpu_debug) and (not ctrl_i.cnt_halt(0))`; for i>=3 `cnt_en(i) <= or_reduce_f(ctrl_i.cnt_event and hpmevent(i)) and (not ctrl_i.cpu_debug) and (not ctrl_i.cnt_halt(i))`. Each counter instance receives this value as `inc_i => cnt_en(i)` in the port map. The RTL therefore establishes cnt_en as the stored per-counter enable that directly controls whether counters advance; corrupting cnt_en changes counting behavior (Integrity).
